land.text: the western half of the Sultanate of Mataram given to Prince Mangkubumi with its capital in Yogyakarta (Treaty of Giyanti, 13 February 1755)

predecessors.note: The Mataram dossier (se-02) lists Yogyakarta as a successor and dates the state from Giyanti too; Cliopatria's row starts in 1744, eleven years early.

land.text: the mancanagara and 'a significant part of its territory', annexed after the Java War; the rump, 'the modern boundary of the Yogyakarta Special Region', stayed under the sultan

successors.note: The sultanate itself continued as a Dutch protectorate state (infobox: 1806-1811 and 1816-1942) and became the Yogyakarta Special Region on 3 August 1950; this dossier ends at the 1830 annexation, as Cliopatria's row does (1829).

capitals.name: Yogyakarta
capitals.note: Mangkubumi 'took the title of Sultan Hamengkubuwono and set up his court in Yogyakarta, not far from Kotagede' (Giyanti page); the Yogyakarta page gives no founding year for the palace.

rulers.name: Hamengkubuwono I (Mangkubumi)
rulers.note: Named Sultan by the Treaty of Giyanti; reigned 1755-1792 (born 6 August 1717, died 4 March 1792).

rulers.name: Hamengkubuwono II
rulers.note: First reign 2 April 1792 - 31 December 1810 (Hamengkubuwono II page; deposed by Daendels in favour of Hamengkubuwono III in December 1810, Java War page footnote). Restored 1811-1812 and 1826-1828, listed below.

rulers.name: Hamengkubuwono II (restored)
rulers.note: Second reign 28 December 1811 - 20 June 1812: 'nearly one year later, in 1811, the English under Stamford Raffles restored him to the throne', then 'in June 1812, he was deposed and exiled to Penang' (Hamengkubuwono II page).

rulers.name: Hamengkubuwono III
rulers.note: Installed by the British on 20 June 1812: '1,200 British troops sacked the Yogyakarta keraton on 20 June 1812, deposing Sultan Hamengkubuwono II in favor of his son Hamengkubuwono III' (Java War page). He died 3 November 1814 (Yogyakarta Sultanate table). His first, short reign is 1810-1811 above.

rulers.name: Hamengkubuwono IV
rulers.note: The Yogyakarta page's table gives 1814-1823 and leaves 1811-1814 and 1826-1855 empty; the gaps are filled from the rulers' own pages and the Java War page.

rulers.name: Hamengkubuwono V
rulers.note: First period 19 December 1823 - 17 August 1826 (Hamengkubuwono V page); the table gives 1823-1826.

rulers.name: Hamengkubuwono II (restored again)
rulers.note: Third reign 20 September 1826 - 3 January 1828 (Hamengkubuwono II page: 'In 1826, the Dutch decided to return him from exile and restored him as the sultan'); the Java War page footnote has the reinstatement on 17 August 1826, the day the Hamengkubuwono V page ends his first period.

rulers.name: Hamengkubuwono V (restored)
rulers.note: Second period 17 January 1828 - 5 June 1855 (Hamengkubuwono V page); this dossier ends in 1830.

correction.text: unchanged Cliopatria outline (12 grid cells, 4,177 km2) but holding from 13 February 1755, not 1744: the state is created by the Treaty of Giyanti; before that the land is Mataram's

keyframe_review.note: Years only. The Yogyakarta infobox gives 3,133 km2 (the present Special Region), ratio 1.33 to Cliopatria's 4,177 km2, within a factor of two. The pages also say the pre-1830 realm was larger than the Special Region: after the Java War 'a significant part of its territory was annexed by the Dutch' and Yogyakarta was left with the modern Special Region boundary. So this outline is the post-1830 core and under-draws 1755-1829; no page opened names the lost districts beyond 'the mancanagara', so no better outline can be written from them (a gap-filler could read Mataram Sultanate/Giyanti sources for Kedu, Bagelen, Banyumas). The Giyanti page gives only 'the western half' of Mataram.

correction.text: unchanged Cliopatria outline, held to 1830, the year the Dutch annexed the mancanagara and the sultan's autonomy was curtailed

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria stops at 1829; the Java War ended in March 1830 and the annexation followed it.

region.text: the western half of Mataram, 'with its capital in Yogyakarta'; the page names no districts

ledger.note: 13 February 1755: the Treaty of Giyanti makes Mangkubumi Sultan Hamengkubuwono I at Yogyakarta. 'the eastern half of the Sultanate of Mataram ... was given to Pakubuwono III with Surakarta as its capital, while the western half was given to Prince Mangkubumi with its capital in Yogyakarta.' Date 'February 13, 1755' (signed and ratified). Region is the researcher's reading (Cliopatria outline) of 'western half'.

1755: the sultanate is born a protectorate of the Dutch East India Company. Infobox: 'De jure protectorate state of the Dutch East India Company (1755-1799)'. The Treaty of Giyanti of 13 February 1755 was made with the Company; the infobox gives only the year, month 2 is the founding month (researcher's reading). The Company has no polity row: the counterpart is the Dutch Republic, whose Cliopatria row holds the Company's Indonesian possessions.
1799: the Company protectorate ends (infobox 1755-1799); the protectorate passes to the Batavian Republic.

1800: Batavian Republic protectorate. Infobox: 'Protectorate state of the Batavian Republic within Dutch East Indies (1800-1806)'. The reviewer wrote that the infobox does not cover 1800-1806; it does, with this line.
1806: the Batavian Republic protectorate ends (infobox 1800-1806); the Kingdom of the Netherlands follows.

1806: protectorate of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Infobox: 'Protectorate state of the Kingdom of the Netherlands within Dutch East Indies (1806-1811; 1816-1942)'. Counterpart dutch-east-indies, the Cliopatria row that carries the Dutch possessions in Java.
1811: the Dutch protectorate lapses when Britain takes Java (infobox 1806-1811).
1811: protectorate of the British East India Company. Infobox: 'Protectorate state of the British East India Company (1811-1816)'. In 1812 the British storm the palace (below).

20 June 1812: British troops storm the palace. 'on 20 June 1812, 1,200 British troops' sacked the Yogyakarta keraton, deposing Sultan Hamengkubuwono II in favour of Hamengkubuwono III; Britain had occupied Java in 1811.

The sack was a single action; the British then held Java until 1816 with Yogyakarta a protectorate of the East India Company (Yogyakarta infobox: 'Protectorate of the British East India Company 1811-1816').

region.text: part of Yogyakarta, 'in some areas' - the Pakualaman enclave at the capital

ledger.note: 1813: the British carve the Duchy of Pakualaman out of the sultanate. Infobox: Pakualaman 'established ... in some areas' in 1813; the Java War page: 'During the four-year occupation, the British split off part of Yogyakarta to form Pakualaman.' Neither page names the land; the 5 km disc is a placeholder at the capital.
1816: the British protectorate ends (infobox 1811-1816); Java returns to the Dutch.

region.text: the mancanagara, the outlying provinces annexed by the Dutch after the Java War

ledger.note: 1830: the Dutch annex the outlying lands. 'The sultanate became the main theatre of military operations during the Java War of 1825-1830. Afterward, a significant part of its territory was annexed by the Dutch, and the degree of autonomy was significantly curtailed.' The Java War page names the 'mancanagara' and leaves Yogyakarta 'the modern boundary of the Yogyakarta Special Region'; the year is that of the war's end (Diponegoro arrested 28 March 1830), not stated for the annexation.

1830: this dossier ends with the Dutch annexation of the mancanagara; the infobox protectorate runs on to 1942 for the rump sultanate, which is not drawn here. The end year is the dossier's, not the infobox's.

region.text: the sultanate's lands under Dutch control after the Java War

ledger.note: 1830: the Dutch take control. The rump princely states 'no longer posed a threat to the Dutch', which now held full control of Javanese lands (Java War page). The sultanate continues as a protectorate state.

wars.name: Java War

zones.text: the sultanate 'the main theatre of military operations'

wars.outcome: Diponegoro rebelled on 21 July 1825 and was arrested at the Dutch Resident's house on 28 March 1830; afterwards the Dutch 'annexed significant proportions of the princely states' remaining territories' (the mancanagara) and the Cultivation System followed.
wars.note: Diponegoro's rebels held no land the pages name, so no rebel dossier is written; a gap-filler may add one (Diponegoro's army, 1825-1830).

wars.name: British occupation of Java and sack of Yogyakarta
wars.outcome: On 20 June 1812 1,200 British troops sacked the palace, deposed Hamengkubuwono II and set up Hamengkubuwono III; in 1813 the British split Pakualaman off Yogyakarta.
wars.note: The war has no article title on the page opened (Wikipedia's 'Invasion of Java (1811)' was not opened); the name is descriptive.

certainty.note: The Giyanti line between 'eastern' and 'western' halves of Mataram, the Pakualaman enclave and the mancanagara have no boundary on the pages opened; all frontiers soft.

sources.note: 13 February 1755; the western half to Mangkubumi at Yogyakarta, the eastern half to Pakubuwono III; the coast ceded in 1743 and 1746. Does not name districts.

sources.title: Java War

sources.title: Hamengkubuwono II
sources.note: Reigns 1792-1810, 1811-1812, 1826-1828; Raffles' restoration, June 1812 deposition, 1826 Dutch restoration.

notes:
Page budget 1-2 per state; three pages were opened (the article, Treaty of Giyanti, Java War), the second and third shared with surakarta-sunanate, because the article gives neither the partition lands nor the 1830 annexation. (1) Cliopatria starts the row in 1744; the state exists from 13 February 1755. 1744-1754 is Mataram (see mataram-sultanate keyframe 1743-1754). (2) The Cliopatria outline equals the post-1830 Special Region core; the 1755-1829 realm was larger but no page opened names the districts (Kedu, Bagelen, Banyumas and the mancanegara are not on these pages) - gap. (3) The sultanate did not end in 1830: it was a protectorate state to 1942 and a Special Region after 1945/1950; the dossier ends at 1830 with Cliopatria, losing about 120 years of a rump state. The protectorates of the infobox are now in this ledger (see REVISION); only Japan 1942-1945 lies outside the dossier. (4) Pakualaman (1813) needs a dossier: counterpart slug 'pakualaman'. (5) Gazetteer name needed: Mancanegara. (6) Disagreement, resolved in the REVISION: the Yogyakarta page's table gives Hamengkubuwono III 1810-1811 with the throne empty 1811-1814; the Hamengkubuwono II page and the Java War page fill it. Capital coordinates from the gazetteer place Yogyakarta. The Giyanti negotiations were held 22-23 September 1754 (Giyanti page). Third Javanese War of Succession (1746-1757) was not opened.

REVISION 2026-10-19 (after review): pages re-opened: Yogyakarta Sultanate, Hamengkubuwono II, Hamengkubuwono V, Java War (four, two beyond the budget of 1-2, because the finding is about dates). (a) Vassal pairs added to this ledger (counterpart = the suzerain, as the reviewer asked, because rule 4 puts both sides in the vassal's ledger): dutch-republic 1755-1799 (the Company has no polity row; the Dutch Republic's Cliopatria row holds its Indonesian possessions), batavian-republic 1800-1806, dutch-east-indies 1806-1811, british-colonial-empire 1811-1816, dutch-east-indies 1816-1830 (the infobox runs to 1942; this dossier ends in 1830). DISAGREEMENT with the reviewer: the review says 'the infobox does not cover 1800-1806'. The Yogyakarta Sultanate infobox does: 'Protectorate state of the Batavian Republic within Dutch East Indies (1800-1806)'. I added that pair, as the Surakarta infobox and the reviewer's own Surakarta finding have it. The 1755 start carries month 2 (the Giyanti month) only so that the ledger order holds; the infobox gives the year alone (confidence 2). (b) Rulers made contiguous from the rulers' own pages: Hamengkubuwono II second reign 28 December 1811 - 20 June 1812 and third 20 September 1826 - 3 January 1828 (Hamengkubuwono II page), Hamengkubuwono III installed 20 June 1812 (Java War) and died 3 November 1814 (Yogyakarta table), Hamengkubuwono V first period 19 December 1823 - 17 August 1826 and second 17 January 1828 - 5 June 1855 (Hamengkubuwono V page). The reviewer's 'Hamengkubuwono IV' dates were not touched: the table has 1814-1823. Page conflict kept: the Java War footnote dates the 1826 reinstatement 17 August, the Hamengkubuwono II page 20 September 1826. (c) Not done, for the gap-fillers named by the reviewer: the Pakualaman land (the Java War page adds only 'a small amount of territory within the region held by the Pakualaman'; the 5 km placeholder stays at confidence 1), the 1755-1829 realm and the mancanagara (no keyframe holds them), Java War contest events with Diponegoro (needs a Diponegoro dossier, se-03-x), the rump sultanate 1830-1950.
